impact:
expandUser (src/context.ts:131-164) applies CPython's posixpath.expanduser on every platform, and bootstrapDeps (src/main-deps.ts:71) consults HOME first — semantics ntpath.expanduser never uses. On Windows (advertised as supported at README.md:58) the port therefore silently resolves a different CODEX_HOME and homeEnc than usage.py whenever HOME is set to anything but USERPROFILE, misattributing every project with both tools exiting 0, and it refuses backslash-separated forms (e.g. CODEX_HOME=~\.codex) and ~user forms that Python expands successfully.

DECISION (owner strategy 2026-08-01: macOS first, Windows/Linux later): the ntpath fix is deferred to the future Windows milestone, where it can be built and verified against a real Windows reference interpreter instead of guessed. What gates T-007 instead is the README half: 0.1.0's platform table must mark Windows/Linux CLI support as experimental with this exact caveat (HOME-vs-USERPROFILE and backslash `~` forms), not advertise parity. Severity stays high until that caveat lands; downgrade to medium once the README is honest, since the remaining defect is then future-platform work on an unshipped surface.
resolution:
PARTIALLY ADDRESSED in T-023 — the README half is done, the code half is deferred by decision.

What landed (2026-08-01): README.md now carries a "Platform support in 0.1.0" table that claims only what was executed. macOS arm64 is the single row marked Verified (the host the parity suite and the package-manager install matrix run on); macOS x64 and Linux are Unverified; Windows is Experimental and carries the exact caveat from this issue — POSIX `~` semantics on every platform, HOME consulted before USERPROFILE so a HOME set to anything else resolves a different CODEX_HOME, and backslash (`CODEX_HOME=~\.codex`) and `~user` forms not expanded at all, with "set CODEX_HOME to an absolute path" given as the workaround. The ccusage-binary-availability table is kept separate and now states explicitly that a binary existing for a platform is not a claim spendbar has been run there.

Severity high -> medium per the decision recorded in the impact above: the package no longer advertises parity it does not have, so the remaining defect is future-platform work on a surface 0.1.0 does not claim to support.

Still open: the ntpath.expanduser behaviour itself (src/context.ts expandUser, src/main-deps.ts bootstrapDeps HOME precedence). Belongs to the Windows milestone, where it can be built and verified against a real Windows reference interpreter rather than guessed. This no longer gates T-007.
title: Windows `~` expansion uses POSIX semantics, diverging from Python's ntpath.expanduser
